diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that we can expand $f_{n}^{j}(\mathbf{h})$ at $\h_{n}:=H_{n}^{j}$ as the following quadratic function
- W_{n}^{T}X^{j} + W_{n}^{T}W_n \tilde{H}^j_n +  (\mathbf{D}^{j}_{n}+\rho\mathbf{I}) (H^{j}-\tilde{H}^j_n)
the updates of MUR is a gradient descent from $\tilde{H}_n$ instead of $H_n$

issues.failure_explanation: The surrogate \eqref{eq:surrogate_MU} is expanded at $\h_n=H_n^j$, but the gradient computation and the MUR formula correspond to the surrogate expanded at $\tilde H_n^j=H_n^j\vee\delta$ (indeed $(D+\rho I)^{-1}(W^TX^j+\rho\tilde H^j_n)$ is the minimizer of the expansion at $\tilde H_n^j$, not at $H_n^j$). Hence whenever $H_n$ has entries below $\delta$, $H_{n+1}$ is not the minimizer of the stated $g_n$, and the surrogate actually minimized is not sharp at the current iterate $H_n$, violating the BMM requirement $g_n(\theta_{n-1})=f_n(\theta_{n-1})$; monotonicity $f(H_{n+1})\le f(H_n)$ then fails. Concretely, for $X=0$, $p=r=N=1$ and positive initialization, MUR iterates converge to $w\approx h\approx\delta$ (fixed point of $h=\rho\delta/(w^2+\rho)$, $w=\rho\delta/(h^2+\rho)$), an interior point with $\nabla f\neq0$, so (iii) fails and the stationarity measure in (i) stays bounded away from zero. (The $W$-update also uses $H_n$ rather than $H_{n+1}$, i.e. a Jacobi rather than the Gauss-Seidel order of Algorithm 1.)

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The function $g_{n}^{(i)}$ in \eqref{eq:BProxLinear} is indeed a majorizing surrogate of $f_{n}^{(i)}$ when the objective $f$ has $L$-Lipschitz gradient and $\lambda \ge L$.
(Majorization) $g_{n}^{(i)}(\theta)- f_{n}^{(i)}(\theta) \ge 0$ for all $\theta \in \Theta^{(i)}$
for each compact subset $\Param_{0}\subseteq \Param$, there exist a constant $L_{f}=L_{f}(\Param_{0})$

issues.failure_explanation: Algorithm 1 and A3(b) require $g_n^{(i)}\ge f_n^{(i)}$ on all of $\Theta^{(i)}$ and $h_n^{(i)}\ge\frac{\rho}{2}\|\theta-\theta_{n-1}^{(i)}\|^2$ globally. With only locally Lipschitz $\nabla f$ on unbounded $\Theta^{(i)}$ (A2 with compact sublevel sets forces superlinear growth, e.g. $f(x)=x^4$), no fixed quadratic prox-linear surrogate majorizes $f_n^{(i)}$ globally for any finite $\lambda$, so the corollary's hypotheses do not place BPGD within Theorem 2.1. Moreover, since the sublevel set and hence the relevant Lipschitz constant depend on $\param_0$, no single 'sufficiently small' step size works for all initializations, and PGD with fixed step diverges from far initializations in such examples; the corollary provides no argument that iterates stay in a region where the local majorization suffices.
